table.name: account
table.purpose: Bank accounts (classic Czech bank dataset): one row per account, with its district, statement frequency, and creation date. Referenced by loans, cards, transactions, orders, and client dispositions.

col_001.name: account_id
col_001.description: Primary key identifying the account; unique across 4500 rows and referenced by loan, disp, trans, and order tables.

col_002.name: district_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to the district lookup table (district.col_001), indicating the geographic district where the account is held (e.g. 35 = Jablonec n. Nisou, 77 = Vsetin).

col_003.name: statement_frequency
col_003.description: Frequency of statement issuance, in Czech: 'POPLATEK MESICNE' = monthly, 'POPLATEK TYDNE' = weekly, 'POPLATEK PO OBRATU' = after each transaction.

col_004.name: created_date
col_004.description: Date the account was created/opened, ranging from 1993-01-01 to 1997-12-29.

table.name: card
table.purpose: Bank payment cards issued to clients (one card per disposition/client), with card type and issue date. Matches the classic Czech bank 'card' table (PK card_id, disp_id, type, issued).

col_001.name: card_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the card; unique integer identifier for each issued card.

col_002.name: disp_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to disp (disposition), linking the card to a client's access on an account; one-to-one with disp/client, so each client holds at most one card.

col_004.name: issued
col_004.description: Date the card was issued (1993-11-07 to 1998-12-29).

table.name: client
table.purpose: Persons (bank customers) of a Czech bank; each row is one client, linked to accounts via the disposition table and to their home district. This matches the classic PKDD'99 Czech bank dataset (districts like 'Jablonec n. Nisou', 'Vyskov').

col_001.name: client_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique client identifier (integer 1-13998, 5369 rows). Referenced by disp (client-account disposition), and by account/loan/order/card tables, indicating those tables carry the client id as a foreign key.

col_003.name: birth_date
col_003.description: Client date of birth (dates 1911-1987, consistent with birth dates of living clients).

col_004.name: district_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to district.col_001; the client's home district (77 Czech districts, lookup labels confirm, e.g. 77 = Vsetin). Joins to card.col_001 and account.col_001 are spurious/coincidental numeric matches, not real relationships.

table.name: disp
table.purpose: Disposition table linking clients to bank accounts, specifying each client's role on the account (owner or disponent/authorized user). One row per client-account relationship. This matches the classic Berka (PKDD'99) financial dataset.

col_001.name: disp_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the disposition record; unique surrogate identifier for each client-account relationship.

col_002.name: client_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to client (client.col_001). One-to-one join accepted by statistics; each disposition belongs to exactly one client.

col_003.name: account_id
col_003.description: Foreign key to account (account.col_001). Many dispositions can point to the same account (4500 distinct accounts for 5369 rows), i.e. an account can have multiple associated clients.

col_004.name: disp_type
col_004.description: Type of disposition: 'OWNER' (account holder, 4500 rows) or 'DISPONENT' (authorized user/additional person on the account, 869 rows).

table.name: district
table.purpose: Demographic and socioeconomic statistics for 77 Czech districts (the classic PKDD'99 financial dataset). One row per district; referenced by clients and accounts as their home district.

col_001.name: district_id
col_001.description: Primary key; sequential district identifier 1-77. Referenced by account and client tables.

col_002.name: district_name
col_002.description: Name of the district (Czech town/district seat, e.g. 'Jablonec n. Nisou', 'Brno - mesto'). Unique per row.

col_003.name: region
col_003.description: Czech region the district belongs to (8 values: Prague, central/north/south/east/west Bohemia, north/south Moravia).

col_004.name: population
col_004.description: District population (42,821 to 1,204,953; Prague is the max outlier).

col_005.name: municipalities_under_500
col_005.description: Count of municipalities in the district with fewer than 500 inhabitants (0-151).

col_008.name: municipalities_over_10000
col_008.description: Count of municipalities with more than 10,000 inhabitants (0-5).

col_009.name: city_count
col_009.description: Small count 1-11 per district, likely the number of cities/towns in the district. Alternative reading: number of urban municipalities; the exact definition cannot be confirmed from values alone.

col_010.name: urban_inhabitants_ratio
col_010.description: Share of population living in urban areas, in percent (33.9-100.0; Prague = 100).

col_011.name: average_salary
col_011.description: Average monthly salary in the district, in CZK (8,110-12,541).

col_012.name: unemployment_rate_1995
col_012.description: Unemployment rate in 1995, in percent (0.2-7.3; one null).

col_013.name: unemployment_rate_1996
col_013.description: Unemployment rate in 1996, in percent (0.43-9.4); values slightly higher than the 1995 column, consistent with year-over-year rates.

col_015.name: crimes_1995
col_015.description: Number of committed crimes in 1995 (818-85,677; Prague is the outlier). One null.

col_016.name: crimes_1996
col_016.description: Number of committed crimes in 1996 (888-99,107); values slightly higher than the 1995 column, consistent with year-over-year counts.

table.name: loan
table.purpose: Loans granted to bank accounts; one row per loan contract, with amount, duration, monthly payment and repayment status. This is the classic PKIC/Financial 'loan' table linked to account via account_id.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to account.col_001; the bank account the loan belongs to. One-to-one here (each account has at most one loan in this dataset).

col_003.name: loan_date
col_003.description: Date the loan was granted (1993-07-05 to 1998-12-08).

col_004.name: amount
col_004.description: Loan principal amount in the local currency (CZK); range 4,980 to 590,820.

col_005.name: duration
col_005.description: Loan duration in months; only values 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 occur. The joins to card/client/disp are spurious coincidences of small integers, not real references.

col_006.name: monthly_payment
col_006.description: Monthly repayment amount; consistent with amount/duration (e.g. 76080/12 = 6340).

col_007.name: status
col_007.description: Loan repayment status code: A = finished contract, no problems; B = finished, not paid / problems; C = running contract, OK; D = running, in debt. Exact per-letter semantics inferred from the standard PKIC coding; the data alone shows only the four values and their frequencies.

table.name: order
table.purpose: Permanent standing payment orders (direct debit / payment orders) from bank accounts, as in the PKDD'99 Czech bank dataset. Each row is one recurring payment order issued by an account to an external bank account, with an amount and a payment category symbol.

col_001.name: order_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the payment order; unique integer identifier.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Owning bank account that issues the payment order; references account.col_001 (many orders per account). The LLM-suggested joins to client/disp are spurious — the statistical join to account is the correct one.

col_003.name: bank_code
col_003.description: Code of the receiving bank (13 anonymized two-letter codes, roughly uniform). Identifies which bank the beneficiary account is held at.

col_004.name: recipient_account_number
col_004.description: Account number of the beneficiary at the receiving bank; near-unique large integers, consistent with anonymized account numbers.

col_005.name: amount
col_005.description: Payment amount in Czech koruna (CZK); positive values from 1 to 14,882, median ~2,596.

col_006.name: payment_symbol
col_006.description: Czech bank payment symbol (k_symbol) categorizing the payment: SIPO = household/utility payments, POJISTNE = insurance, UVER = loan repayment, LEASING = leasing; empty string = no symbol/other.

table.name: trans
table.purpose: Bank account transaction records (PKDD'99 Czech financial dataset). One row per transaction on an account, with amount, resulting balance, operation type, and characterization. Czech labels throughout.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Owning account; references account.col_001 (many transactions per account).

col_004.name: transaction_type
col_004.description: Transaction type in Czech: PRIJEM = income/credit, VYDAJ = expense/debit, VYBER = cash withdrawal (recorded as debit).

col_005.name: operation
col_005.description: Operation mode in Czech: VYBER = cash withdrawal, VYBER KARTOU = card withdrawal, VKLAD = cash deposit, PREVOD NA UCET = transfer to another account (outgoing), PREVOD Z UCTU = transfer from another account (incoming). Null when type is VYBER (redundant with col_004).

col_006.name: amount
col_006.description: Transaction amount in Czech koruna (CZK); min 0, max 87,400, median 2,100.

col_007.name: balance
col_007.description: Account balance in CZK after the transaction; can be negative (min -41,126).

col_008.name: transaction_characterization
col_008.description: Bank's characterization of the transaction in Czech: UROK = interest credited, SLUZBY = bank services fee, SIPO = household/utility payment, DUCHOD = pension, SANKC. UROK = sanction (penalty) interest, POJISTNE = insurance, UVER = loan payment. Blank/null when not characterized.

col_009.name: partner_bank
col_009.description: Code of the partner bank for inter-bank transfers (two-letter codes, e.g. QR, AB, ST). Null for non-transfer transactions.

col_010.name: partner_account
col_010.description: Partner account number for inter-bank transfers (large integers up to ~99,994,199; 0 also occurs). Null for non-transfer transactions.
